text: Gordon had nine points in 27 minutes as a starter. The show said his usage rate has dropped and he has fallen off this season.
Aaron Gordon played just 24 minutes in Denver's loss, and the show is comfortable moving on from him.
Aaron Nesmith played 33 minutes as a starter on November 13. The show said he stays worth rostering until Tyrese Haliburton returns.
The show said Aaron Nesmith has a secure starting role and can play 34 minutes, though some nights he plays closer to 28. He started and played 33 and 36 minutes in his last two games.
Nesmith scored two points on 14 percent shooting in 29 minutes. The show said he really struggles with Tyrese Haliburton out and is hard to trust right now.

Atlanta started Wiggins on 11/18 with Kingston Flemings out, and he played 26 minutes while RayJ Dennis played only 10 off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker played 32 minutes in that game, and the show called that a role he should keep.

Dan Besbris listed Aaron Wiggins as a top-100 season-long pickup because CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings are out, which opens up minutes for him. Wiggins played 26 minutes in his last game on 11/18.

Bailey was held to 8 shots on Nov. 17, and his minutes fell to 23 after he played 29 to 35 minutes in his prior games. The show said he should stay rostered while Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen are out for another two or three weeks. Bailey bounced back to 27 minutes and 19 points on Nov. 18.
Dan Besbris listed Ace Bailey as a top-100 season-long pickup because Jaren Jackson Jr. is out, which opens up minutes for him. Bailey played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/18.
Mara moved back into the starting lineup and Kenrich Williams went to the bench. Mara played 27 minutes with eight assists, and the show said to keep rolling with him.
Dan Besbris listed Aday Mara as a top-100 season-long pickup because Chet Holmgren is out, which opens up minutes for him. Mara played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/18.

The show said AJ Dybantsa is a tough play at $6,600 because he shares the scoring load with Kyshawn George, Anthony Davis and Trae Young. Dybantsa had 13 points and 23.5 DK points in 34 minutes on Nov 11.

AJ Dybantsa scored 12.2 of his 28.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 28-point loss against HOU on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
AJ Dybantsa scored 16 points on 18 shots with a high usage rate. The show said his production has been middling and his shooting has been poor.

AJ Dybantsa has started every game and played 30 to 44 minutes over his last eight games. The show said he is off his minutes limit and should play close to 40 minutes against Memphis, and it preferred him to Kyshawn George.

Dybantsa played 38 minutes and posted 23 points and 12 rebounds on 11/18 while making no threes. The show said he scores by getting to the rim and likes his 11/20 matchup against a Chicago team that it says allows the most paint points in the league.

Ajay Mitchell is starting for an Oklahoma City team missing Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, and he played 28 minutes on 11/10. The show said nobody is coming to take his role soon because the Thunder are so injured.

Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, and Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams at the Clippers. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored 26 to 31 points in each of his last four games.
Ajay Mitchell returned from a sprained ankle on November 15 after missing the November 13 game, and he started and played 27 minutes. The show called him a full start going forward.
Al Horford sat Monday, Nov. 2, for rest on the second night of a back-to-back, not an injury, and is available Thursday.

Al Horford started over Will Richard, but he went scoreless in 14 minutes and came off the bench in the second half. Charles Bassey started the second half instead, and the show said Steve Kerr will keep mixing lineups.

Horford has started two of Golden State's last five games but has played only 13, 15, 21, 10 and 14 minutes in that span, including 14 minutes in his start on 11/16. The show said his minimum $3,500 price is the only thing making him a value, and it said it would rather see Charles Bassey or De'Anthony Melton start.

Caruso returned on Nov. 4 after missing four games and played 20 minutes off the bench with seven points. The show said he should carve out his own role with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams likely out for the season and Chet Holmgren sidelined.

Alex Caruso moved into the starting lineup with Ajay Mitchell out and played 29 minutes on a back-to-back for 14 points, seven rebounds, three steals, and four threes. Kenrich Williams went to the bench. The show said Ajay Mitchell's ankle injury may not be significant, and Mitchell and Jalen Williams will cut into Caruso's role when they return.

The show listed Alex Caruso as a short-term pickup while Ajay Mitchell is out. With Mitchell sidelined by a right ankle sprain, Caruso started on November 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 minutes on November 13 when Kenrich Williams started.

Caruso started on Nov 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 and 18 minutes in his next two games. The show said a lot of guard minutes are up for grabs in Oklahoma City, so it would hold him through a bad game.
Alex Caruso played only 9 minutes because he could not finish the game. The show said his inability to last through games is the main problem with trusting him.

Alex Caruso was moved from questionable to out for tonight (right hip soreness) on the NBA's 06:15 PM injury report. He had averaged 20 minutes over his last 5 games, so those minutes go to teammates; the injury page lists who gains.
Alex Karaban played 29 minutes and went scoreless while Sacramento was without Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter. The show called him the worst pick in his draft class.
Alex Morales played 29 minutes off the bench Tuesday at Sacramento with Paolo Banchero, Jalen Suggs, Jonathan Isaac and Tristan da Silva all out.
Alex Morales, a two-way player, made his first NBA start after Jamal Cain was injured. He played 18 minutes and scored five points. Jase Richardson stayed on the bench for 20 minutes.
He is questionable with left knee soreness, and Deandre Ayton started at center in his place Monday and played 24 minutes.

Alex Sarr started and played 44 minutes in the double-overtime loss to Detroit, posting 30 points and 9 rebounds for 51.25 DraftKings points. The show said he played more mainly because Kyshawn George fouled out, not because Anthony Davis fouled out late.

Alex Sarr played 27 minutes on November 15 with the rest of Washington's starting lineup intact. The show said 27 minutes is the expected number for him and that he has come around after a slow start.
Alex Sarr scored 25 points with three blocks after scoring 30 points in his previous game. The show said his usage has gone up after a poor start, though his shooting will not stay this hot.
Alex Sarr (illness) and Tre Johnson (low back soreness) are questionable against Houston, which would open minutes for Bilal Coulibaly.

Alex Sarr had a poor line but still played 31 minutes as Washington lost its eighth straight game. The show said his overall activity has been trending up and that the playing time is the part to trust.
Alex Sarr played just 22 minutes but still posted a useful line. The show said his minutes have been all over the place this season.
Graves played 31 minutes off the bench with Barrett and Barnes out, which was far more than his usual 13 to 18 minutes. The show liked seeing the team trust him but is not adding him.
He missed Friday with low back soreness, and Clint Capela started at center with 11 rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes. Houston has not posted its injury report for Saturday yet.

The show said Alperen Sengun has an easy matchup on Nov 13 because Utah is without Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic, leaving Mo Bamba and Jaxson Hayes to guard him. Houston's own centers Clint Capela and Steven Adams are still out.

Houston is without Clint Capela and Steven Adams, and Marcus Smart is serving a league suspension. Alperen Sengun has played 35 to 39 minutes in three of his last four games, but Houston is a 17.5-point favorite over a Utah team missing Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

Alperen Sengun played 28 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 8 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 45.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Alperen Sengun left Wednesday's win at Indiana with a swollen right eye and a scratched left cornea. Houston did not say whether he will miss time before Friday at Denver, and Steven Adams opened the second half at center.
Sengun is questionable for Friday at Denver with an eye injury from Wednesday's game against Indiana, and Clint Capela is already out.
Sengun is questionable at Denver with an eye injury, and Clint Capela is out and Steven Adams is questionable, so Houston's center spot is the key late-slate decision.
Amen Thompson had 19 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two blocks in 29 minutes. The show said it still wants more playing time for him, but the game was not close late.

Amen Thompson ran the point for Houston on November 15 with Fred VanVleet resting and Marcus Smart suspended, and he played 29 minutes with 26 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. The show said he is much more productive when he is the point guard, but his role has not been that this season. VanVleet returned on November 16.

Amen Thompson played 29 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 49.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Thompson returned after missing one game with soreness, and that sent Tari Eason back to the bench. The show said Thompson looks much better than he did a couple of weeks ago, though sharing the ball with Fred VanVleet limits his ceiling.

Andre Drummond has played 12 to 16 minutes off the bench in each of his last six games. The show said he can produce 30 fantasy points in 18 minutes but is only a large-field tournament dart, especially if Cup-game minutes tighten.

Nembhard is questionable for Friday at Cleveland with a left hip sprain after missing two games, and Rick Carlisle said the absence should not be long. Quenton Jackson has started at point guard in his place.

Dan Besbris listed Andrew Nembhard as a top-100 season-long pickup because Tyrese Haliburton is out (Nembhard himself is currently injured), which opens up minutes for him. Nembhard played 34 minutes in his last game on 11/13.

Nembhard is questionable at Cleveland with a hip sprain after missing two games; Rick Carlisle said it should not be a long absence. Quenton Jackson has started in his place with Tyrese Haliburton also out.
The show said Andrew Wiggins picked up most of Pelle Larsson's playing time on November 13, although he did not do much with it. Wiggins played 32 minutes off the bench and scored 8 points.

Andrew Wiggins has come off the bench since 11/08 after starting earlier in the month. The show said he has complained to the media about his role and that Pelle Larsson's absence could flip his minutes back up over time.

Andrew Wiggins played 34 minutes off the bench with Bam Adebayo leaving early and Pelle Larsson out, and he scored 17 points with three blocks. The show noted he took only nine shots and doubted he would do much more even if Adebayo misses time.
Anfernee Simons played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble and had 12 points with nothing else. The show said he is a hot-and-cold scorer who does not fit well on a good team.

Anfernee Simons moved into the starting lineup with Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown both out, and he played 38 minutes for 18 points. The show said Simons is playable mostly for points and threes only if both Maxey and Brown sit again.

Anthony Black started and played 37 minutes but scored just 5 points for 19 DraftKings points against Milwaukee. The show called it a long overdue clunker after an intense hot streak and said he is still a play.

Anthony Black had 20 points and 7 assists in 33 minutes against Boston on 11/16 in Jalen Suggs' first game back in the starting lineup. The show said it never expected Suggs' return to hurt Black much.

Anthony Black is carrying a big usage load while Paolo Banchero is out, but he had a rare off night with missed free throws and a poor shooting line on 16 shots. The show said Black's numbers should come down further when Banchero returns and his steals, blocks and free throw rate regress.
Dan Besbris listed Anthony Black as a top-75 season-long pickup because Paolo Banchero is out, which opens up minutes for him. Black played 37 minutes in his last game on 11/18.
The show said new Orlando coach Sean Sweeney plays his core players a lot of minutes. Black has played 33 to 37 minutes in each of Orlando's last three games.
He missed Friday with his ankle sprain, and the show doubts he plays both games of the back-to-back that continues Saturday at Oklahoma City.

He has missed two straight games with his ankle sprain and is questionable again at Detroit. Kyshawn George scored 33 and 38.25 DK points in the two games without him, and the show expects George to be the most popular play if Davis sits.
Anthony Davis had 21 points and 13 rebounds in 34 minutes Wednesday, and Washington hosts Detroit on the second night of a back-to-back. The Wizards have not posted their injury report yet.

Anthony Davis has played legitimate starter minutes lately, with 35 and 34 minutes in his last two games and a 44-minute game on 11/12. The show said he is producing about 1.33 DraftKings points per minute and called his 11/20 matchup against a fast, poor Chicago defense the best spot among the top-salary players.
Anthony Edwards remained out on 11/14 and has not played since 10/26. The show said he will be out a long while and does not expect anything to change for Minnesota until he returns.

Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo are ruled out again for Chicago's visit. Ayo Dosunmu keeps starting, and Minnesota is a 14.5-point favorite against a Bulls team on the second night of a back-to-back.
He is ruled out tonight.
He is ruled out tonight (arthroscopic procedure on his right knee).

Minnesota is again without Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark against the Knicks, and Jonathan Kuminga is questionable with a right shoulder contusion. When Kuminga sat Tuesday, Trey Lyles played 31 minutes off the bench.
Asa Newell had surgery Tuesday to repair a plantar plate tear in his left big toe, hurt November 4. He will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Thompson played 43 minutes and posted his first triple-double on November 12, but he played only 18 minutes on November 14. The show said he has a very large role whenever games are competitive and he stays out of foul trouble.

Ausar Thompson has not made a three-pointer all season, but he averaged 3.3 steals and 1.7 blocks over his last three games through 11/17, and he added 12 assists in 29 minutes on 11/17. The show said he looks like he has finally been freed up after years of blood-clot problems and has a green light, though it called him a sell-high because a top-five pace will not last.

Austin Reaves is ruled out at Phoenix with a left heel bruise (X-rays negative, day-to-day). Collin Sexton is questionable after stitches over his eye, while Quentin Grimes is available with a splint on his finger.
He is ruled out tonight. Grimes is the main beneficiary and could post top-70 numbers in those games.
He is questionable tonight vs UTA.
Reaves is ruled out for Friday against Sacramento, his fourth straight missed game, with a heel bruise and bone bruise from Nov. 11. JJ Redick said there is nothing structural beyond the bruise.

Ayo Dosunmu has been Minnesota's starter with Anthony Edwards out, and Edwards has not played since 10/26 after a knee arthroscopy. Dosunmu played 39 minutes on 11/17 and has scored at least 24 points in four of his last six games. The show said the Edwards injury turned his season around and guessed he has about two more months in this role.
The show said Ayo Dosunmu has had two bad games in his last three. He scored 6 points on 9 shots in 32 minutes on November 19 after an 8-point game on November 16.
Dan Besbris listed Ayo Dosunmu as a top-50 season-long pickup because Anthony Edwards is out, which opens up minutes for him. Dosunmu played 32 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

Miller has moved into a real bench role with 20 minutes and 12 points on Nov. 8 and 16 minutes and 13 points on Nov. 10, after playing 12 or fewer minutes in each prior game. The show called him impressive and is watching how the Clippers find minutes for him.
Bam Adebayo played 34 minutes on Nov. 8 and 37 minutes on Nov. 10. The show said he was awful to start the season but has picked it up while playing huge minutes, and it called him fairly priced.

The show said Bam Adebayo's usage rate is down about four points from last year while playing next to Giannis Antetokounmpo, and that his points and rebounds are lower. He is averaging about 2.2 steals per game through November 11, which the show called a likely mirage that will come back down.

The show said Bam Adebayo has rebuilt his game this season by mostly dropping his three-point attempts and working around the rim, which has pushed his field goal percentage to about 53 percent. It said his high steal rate is driving much of his fantasy value and could fall.

Bam Adebayo played 16 minutes in a 18-point win against HOU on Monday, 20 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 11 minutes of garbage time. His 11.8 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Bam Adebayo sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness; Miami called it proactive and does not think it is long-term. Giannis Antetokounmpo moved to center and Andrew Wiggins started the second half. Miami next plays Wednesday.

Scheierman started and played 29 minutes on 11/11 with Paul George out. The show said that game is why his recent rank looks good, since he played only 11 minutes in the next game and has stayed in a small bench role since George returned.

Baylor Scheierman played 18 minutes off the bench on November 15 and had 12 points and two steals. The show said Boston's bench minutes can go to Scheierman, Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez or Jordan Walsh on any given night, which makes any of them hard to trust.

Baylor Scheierman scored 19.2 of his 27.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 37-point win against DAL on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
Baylor Scheierman played only 11 minutes and scored zero points one game after a strong night, so the show admitted its call on him did not work.
Ben Sheppard is having surgery Wednesday to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee.
Ben Simmons is out for the season.
The show said Benedict Mathurin gets a bump with Dejounte Murray out while Murray waits to be traded. The show framed it as a deeper-league bump rather than a major role change.

The rookie has averaged about 22 minutes and 12 points from Oct. 29 through Nov. 10, and the show said Oklahoma City is using him more than most people expected. The show said the addition of Nique Clifford and the eventual return of Jalen Williams will cut into his minutes.
Bilal Coulibaly returned on Nov. 11 after missing Nov. 9 and played 25 minutes off the bench. The show said he is off the injury report and offers steals, blocks and a few assists.

Bobby Portis played 23 minutes after Bam Adebayo left with hip tightness, up from 14 to 20 minutes in his previous six games. The show said Portis is Miami's only other true center and should get at least 26 to 28 minutes if Adebayo sits, which has typically made him fantasy viable.

Bones Hyland has played 21 to 23 minutes in his last two games with Anthony Edwards out, up from 10 to 13 minutes earlier in the month. The show said Jaylen Clark's injury on November 14 and blowouts helped him, and it does not think his recent efficiency is sustainable.

The show said Bones Hyland should get 16 to 20 minutes off the bench while Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark are out. He played 23 and 21 minutes in his two games before Monday, but only 13 minutes on Monday night. The show said his strong recent numbers will not hold long term.

Hyland played 17 minutes on 11/17 and has played between 13 and 23 minutes in each of his last four games. The show said Minnesota keeps him around 15 to 16 minutes no matter who is in or out, which makes him riskier as his price rises to $4,500.
Smith has been in and out of the rotation, but he started the second half over Quenton Jackson on Wednesday and played 18 minutes. The show said it cannot trust him to play enough most nights.
Bradley Beal (knee) has not played yet this season and is still recovering.

The show said Brandin Podziemski will be great with Stephen Curry out. Per the show, last season he averaged 17.5 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.9 assists per 36 minutes with Curry off the floor, and this season's smaller sample is 18.2 points and 5.7 assists per 36. The show suggested taking about 10 percent off those rates as a fair expectation.

Brandin Podziemski is starting and playing about 30 minutes a night without Stephen Curry, but he scored only 10 points on Nov. 18. The show said it expected him to break out with Curry out and called his production a disappointment.

Golden State lost 126-98 at Memphis, which was its fourth straight blowout loss without Stephen Curry, who is out with a right oblique tear. The show said Brandin Podziemski is showing how hard it is to play without the open looks Curry creates for him.

Brandon Ingram (heel surgery) and Bradley Beal are out again for the Clippers. Darius Garland is playing through a back issue, and Keaton Wagler has played 25 to 28 minutes off the bench in each of his last three games.
The show said Brandon Ingram might be back for the Clippers' next game. His return would cut into minutes for wings like Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr. and Keaton Wagler.
He is ruled out tonight (right heel surgery). Wagler becomes the second scoring option behind Garland.

He is out Monday with a hip strain, Kon Knueppel is out at least four more weeks and Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. Moussa Diabate is questionable, and the show named Hannes Steinbach as the fill-in if he sits.

Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder are all out at Phoenix, while Moussa Diabate and Grant Williams are probable. Sion James and Grayson Allen started Monday, and Allen scored 27 points with six threes.
Brandon Miller is off the injury report after missing two games with a hip strain, with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder still out with hamstring strains.

Brandon Miller played 24 minutes on 11/15 in his return from injury and 32 minutes on 11/17. The show said Charles Lee explained after the 11/17 game that he kept Miller out of overtime to manage him as he comes back from the injury, so his minutes are still being watched.

Brandon Williams has a mild left hamstring strain and is out at least a week. Golden State is also without Jimmy Butler III, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II at Houston, which is missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams.

The Warriors announced that Brandon Williams has returned to on-court activity and will be re-evaluated on Saturday, 11/21, so he is out at least until then. The show said his return would cut into LJ Cryer's role as the backup point guard, and Cryer has started on 11/16 and 11/18 while Williams has been out.
Brayden Burries has kept starting for Milwaukee, but his minutes have ranged from 19 to 29. The show said his role depends on whether he plays well enough for the team to keep him on the floor.

Brayden Burries started and played 29 minutes on November 15 in a game where starters Tyler Herro, Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma played 20 to 23 minutes. The show said his minutes go up in blowouts while the veterans' minutes go down, which gives him a relatively safe floor.

Brayden Burries scored 20 points on nine shots in 25 minutes and has started the last nine games. He has reached 30 minutes only once in that stretch, and the show said Taylor Jenkins will not play guys 33 minutes, which limits his value.

Brayden Burries started again on November 19 and played 28 minutes, and he has now started all 10 games he has played in November. The show said he keeps starting but does not offer much across all categories.

Brice Sensabaugh jumped to 23 and 27 minutes in his last two games after playing 10 to 14 minutes in his previous five. The show said it does not firmly believe the bump will last because Will Hardy keeps changing his bench groups, and it called him a risky scoring stream who could still drop back to about 14 minutes.

Sensabaugh's bench minutes have climbed to 23, 27 and 30 over his last three games while Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out. The show said Utah does not have many options and that he has a real NBA skill, although it hoped he would draw less ownership on 11/17.

Sensabaugh's minutes climbed in every game from 11/6 to 11/17 (10, 13, 14, 23, 27, 30, 35), and he scored 40 points with eight threes off the bench in 35 minutes on 11/17. The show tied the jump to Lauri Markkanen being out of the lineup (Markkanen has not played since 11/6) and said Sensabaugh is filling that scoring gap. The box score shows his minutes fell back to 14 on 11/18 when Jaxson Hayes returned, so the trend is not locked in.
Brice Sensabaugh played only 14 bench minutes after a hot scoring game. The show said he has a limited fantasy game and that his big night was a hot shooting game off the bench, not a new role.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.

Lopez scored 26 points on 11-of-21 shooting in the Clippers' 113-112 win over Oklahoma City on Nov. 13. The show said that was the first time all season he took more than 11 shots in a game. The show credited the 38-year-old with working his way back into a real role at about 24 minutes a night.

Brook Lopez has started at center ahead of Isaiah Jackson in every game since at least November 8, and he scored 26 points on November 13. The show said the switch to the starting lineup sparked his run, but it expects the frontcourt to get crowded when Yanic Konan Niederhauser returns from foot surgery.

Brook Lopez played 29 minutes on November 15 and had eight assists even though he shot poorly. The show said he was the only Clippers starter who held up in that game, finishing plus two. The show called him the clearest hold among the Clippers starters.

The show said Lopez has been humming along since he moved into the Clippers' starting lineup, and he has started every game since Nov. 2. It said he is top 50 in fantasy over the last week but worried that the fun may not last on a losing team.

Brook Lopez played 23 minutes in a 25-point loss against UTA on Tuesday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 39.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said Brook Lopez is not washed and continues to play well. He scored 23 points with five threes on November 19 after 23 points in his previous game.

Buddy Hield played 25 minutes off the bench on November 13 and stayed on the floor late while playing well. The show said Chicago will need bench production without Caleb Wilson and called him a stream option on light days.

Buddy Hield had been out of Chicago's rotation behind Jordan Hawkins, but he played 25 and 20 minutes on November 13 and 14 after Caleb Wilson went down. The show said his usage is up, but it does not trust his three-point shooting to hold.

The show said Cade Cunningham carries about a 30% usage rate and a 38% assist rate this season with about 56.5% true shooting. It projected him at about 51 DK points on 11/12 and called him the best stud play on the slate even though Washington plays at a slow pace.
Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both ruled out at Miami. Cade Cunningham played 48 minutes Thursday and scored 52 points, and Paul Reed played 38 minutes at center.
Cunningham is probable for Friday against Toronto with right knee soreness after skipping the second night of a back-to-back Wednesday.
Cunningham is probable with right knee soreness after resting Wednesday, and Detroit is still without Jalen Duren and Duncan Robinson.

Martin started and played 33 and 34 minutes on 11/14 and 11/15 while Max Christie did not play. The show asked whether his minutes bump was tied to blowouts or to Christie's absence and was not interested. Christie returned on 11/18 for 8 minutes, and Martin played 20 minutes as a starter.

Caleb Martin played 20 minutes in a 22-point win against GSW on Wednesday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 21.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
Caleb Wilson played only 15 minutes on November 11 and has missed Chicago's last two games. The show said he went down, which opened minutes for Patrick Williams and Buddy Hield.
Cam Johnson was out on Oct. 28 and is expected to return fairly soon.
Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. are both questionable Saturday against Sacramento. Spencer has moved ahead of Pippen in the rotation and had eight assists in 23 minutes Thursday.

With Ty Jerome out again with a hip injury (Jerome has not played since 11/13), Spencer has started and played 34 and 32 minutes on 11/14 and 11/16. He had nine assists on 11/16. The show called him the main guard while Jerome is out and a start in standard leagues.

Cam Spencer should start again Wednesday because Ty Jerome is out. In the two games Jerome missed, Spencer started and played 34 and 32 minutes for 34.3 and 33.0 DraftKings points. Off the bench before that, he played 17 to 24 minutes.

Cam Spencer has been starting for Memphis while Ty Jerome is out with a hip injury, and he scored 26 points with five threes in 29 minutes on Nov. 18. The show said there is still no clear timeline for Jerome, who has not played since Nov. 13, so Spencer's lead guard role could last anywhere from days to a month.

Cam Spencer has started all four games Ty Jerome has missed, playing 27 to 34 minutes in those starts after playing 20 to 24 minutes off the bench before. The show said his all-around upside makes him the better short-term option over Julian Champagnie while Jerome is out.
Dan Besbris listed Cam Spencer as a top-75 season-long pickup because Ty Jerome is out, which opens up minutes for him. Spencer played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

Cameron Boozer played 25 minutes in a 31-point win against NOP on Friday, 9 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 36.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Cameron Boozer has started every game, but his minutes have slipped from 33 in his 11/9 and 11/11 games to 25 and 29 in his last two. The show said his shooting efficiency has been among the worst of the rookie class, but it liked him as a bounce-back with Ty Jerome out.

Cameron Boozer made seven threes and scored 29 points on 11/16, but he played only 29 minutes because Memphis was comfortably ahead. The show said he normally settles into a 32 to 33 minute role and liked him against Cleveland with Evan Mobley out and Ty Jerome out on his own side.

With Ty Jerome out on Monday, Cameron Boozer took on more of the scoring and set a season high with 29 points, making 7 of 13 threes, including two during the 10-0 third-quarter run that tied the game.
Boozer has played 29, 29 and 28 minutes in his last three games, including competitive ones. The show said the minutes cap is frustrating but that he still has a strong ceiling and floor at $8,400.

Memphis is short again at Cleveland: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about three months. Boozer, Cam Spencer and Jerami Grant carry more of the load.
Boozer had 18 points, eight rebounds, five assists and four steals on Wednesday, and he led Memphis in DraftKings points. The show said he is cooking right now.
Cameron Carr made his debut Sunday and played 1 minute late in the game without scoring.
Cameron Johnson picked up five fouls and still played 27 minutes, but he had nine points and no rebounds. The show said to move on from him.
LeVert played for the first time this season on Wednesday and scored eight points in eight minutes. He is another name in a crowded Milwaukee guard rotation.
Caris LeVert played the final 11 minutes of the November 19 game and was in Milwaukee's closing lineup. The show could not explain the choice, which adds to the Bucks' rotation chaos.

Carter Bryant scored 14.5 of his 15.8 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 38-point win against GSW on Friday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
